_problem:
A session row with visibility='public' and slots_max IS NULL is an INVALID STATE that the database currently permits. PRD E#7 (quoted at feature_session_management_tech.md:120) makes public sessions require finite capacity; NULL means unlimited and is only valid for non-public. The invariant is enforced today only at the SessionService validation choke-point, so any writer that bypasses it — a fixture, a legacy row, a direct SQL write, a future service — creates a row nothing rejects.

Why that matters beyond tidiness: Verdict 20 recorded this as an ENABLEMENT_ONLY gate blocking the public-discovery projector, and the reason is that the invalid state is INVISIBLE TO EVENT-DRIVEN REPAIR. feature_marketplace_discovery_tech.md edge #15 says an invalid row must be skipped, its stale projection purged and an audit emitted — but that handling only runs when the projector EVALUATES the session. Flipping an already-projected public session from finite slots_max to NULL by a bypassing writer emits no session event, so the projector never revisits it and a stale-but-now-invalid projection stays PUBLICLY VISIBLE. Unit test #26 places such a row into a batch by hand, so it proves behaviour-when-reached, not that every invalid row is reached. The periodic sweep does time-based expiry only.

The backlog entry for this gap listed three candidates and directed that (c), the DB CHECK, be evaluated FIRST because it is the cheapest and most fail-closed: it removes the invalid state at the source, which may make the durable-invalidation-event and the periodic-reconciliation candidates unnecessary rather than merely deferred. This slice is that evaluation, carried to a migration.
_decision_contract: feature_session_management_tech.md:120 already names the exact predicate and its status: `NOT (visibility='public' AND slots_max IS NULL)` is a 'hardening candidate qua migration mới monotonic nếu chốt — cùng pattern DD-45a §4, chưa thuộc scope slice nào'. This slice does not invent the constraint; it decides whether to land it and does so under the repo's existing expand-only migration discipline. The column stays NULLABLE — unlimited remains valid for non-public sessions, and narrowing the column would be a different, breaking change. The two existing CHECKs on sessions (sessions_vis_chk, sessions_slots_chk at schema.ts:602 and :601) are neither weakened nor replaced; this adds a third alongside them and follows their naming convention. Migrations 0000-0023 stay byte-identical.
_scope_in: One module, packages/db. Exactly ONE monotonic migration after the live tail (0024 at authoring baseline 0023) adding the capacity-visibility CHECK to sessions, using whatever add-then-validate shape the design probe pins for existing data; the schema.ts mirror alongside the other sessions CHECKs; and real-role tests proving the constraint rejects the invalid state and accepts every valid one.
_scope_out: NO projector, no TypeScript runtime, no apps/bot change — this slice runs in PARALLEL with job-schedule-outbox-dispatch and any file it shares with apps/bot would collide. NO change to public_sessions' shape, and specifically NOT the eight missing DD-41 discovery fields or the stale skillLevel column recorded at feature_marketplace_discovery_tech.md:28,60 — that drift is real and separate. NO column narrowing: slots_max stays nullable. NO weakening or replacement of sessions_vis_chk or sessions_slots_chk. NO edit to applied migrations 0000-0023. NO change to RLS policies, roles, or grants. NO decision on candidates (a) durable invalidation event or (b) periodic reconciliation — this slice's outcome INFORMS that decision and must not pre-empt it; if the CHECK lands cleanly, say so and let the owner close or re-scope the parent backlog item.
_design_probe:
Required per canonical autopilot-prompt-GENERIC v0.6.1 §0.1 — trigger (7) schema/migration and (6) amends a merged core table. Before any production edit, write .autopilot/state/db-public-visibility-capacity-check/design-probe.md pinning FOUR things and STOP for founder confirm.

(a) EXISTING VIOLATING ROWS — the question this slice exists to answer, and the one a mechanical mirror will get wrong by writing `ADD CONSTRAINT ... NOT VALID` followed immediately by `VALIDATE CONSTRAINT` and assuming that is the safe expand-only idiom. It is not, here: NOT VALID skips existing rows, VALIDATE then scans them and FAILS if any violate. Two statements in one migration therefore have exactly the same failure mode as adding the constraint outright, while LOOKING careful. Measure first — count rows where visibility='public' AND slots_max IS NULL, in whatever environments are reachable — then pin one of: validate in the same migration because the count is provably zero and a test enforces it stays zero; add NOT VALID only and defer VALIDATE to a later slice with a documented remediation step; or remediate in-migration, which needs an explicit owner decision about what a public unlimited session should BECOME. Do not pick the shape that looks safest; pick the one whose failure mode you can state.

(b) LOCK AND DURATION. ADD CONSTRAINT takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on sessions; VALIDATE takes a weaker SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE but scans the table. State the expected impact against realistic row counts and whether a lock_timeout guard belongs in the migration.

(c) THE SEAM WITH THE SERVICE CHOKE-POINT. feature_session_management_tech.md:386 makes join fail-closed on this exact invalid state, at a choke-point described as covering every branch below it. Once the DB rejects the state, that handling becomes unreachable-by-construction rather than load-bearing. Pin explicitly whether it stays (defence in depth, and the honest answer while any environment is unmigrated) or is removed — and if it stays, say so in the spec so a later reader does not delete it as dead code.

(d) WHAT THIS CLOSES AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. The parent backlog item names three candidates. State precisely which failure modes the CHECK eliminates and which survive it — in particular whether a row that was ALREADY projected before this migration can still be serving a stale public projection, since the CHECK prevents new invalid rows but does not purge an existing projection. If anything survives, name it; do not let 'evaluate (c) first' silently become 'the gap is closed'.
_acceptance: PVC-1: inserting or updating a session to visibility='public' with slots_max IS NULL is REJECTED by the database — assert by attempting both paths (insert, and update of an existing private-unlimited row to public), not by reading the catalog.

PVC-2: every VALID combination still succeeds — public with finite slots_max, private with finite slots_max, and private with NULL slots_max. The third is the one a too-broad constraint would break, and unlimited-private is explicitly still supported.
PVC-3: sessions_vis_chk and sessions_slots_chk still exist and still reject their original violation cases — assert by attempting the violations, not by reading the catalog alone.
PVC-4: migrations 0000-0023 are byte-identical after 0024 applies, and the migration-count assertions advance 24 -> 25 in BOTH places that assert them.
PVC-5: schema.ts mirrors the new CHECK alongside the existing sessions constraints and follows the sessions_*_chk naming convention.

PVC-6: whatever validation shape the probe pinned in item (a) is actually what shipped, and its stated failure mode is exercised — if the claim is 'zero violating rows', a test must seed one, prove the migration or the constraint rejects it, and clean up. A migration that would fail on real data must not pass its own test suite on empty data.
PVC-7: no RLS policy, role or grant changed; no column narrowed. Assert structurally against the migration diff.
PVC-8: full workspace suite green; the DB suite count increases only by the tests this slice adds.
_scope_exception: Runs in PARALLEL with job-schedule-outbox-dispatch (2026-07-27 owner decision). Disjointness was verified rather than assumed: this slice is packages/db only with invariants [schema, marketplace]; that slice is apps/bot only with invariants [retry-liveness]. Empty file intersection and empty invariant intersection, so scripts/autopilot-scope-gate:186-193 raises neither SCOPE_COLLISION. Note that the parent backlog item job-infra-public-projection-reconciliation declares invariants [retry-liveness, marketplace] — this slice deliberately drops retry-liveness because candidate (c) involves no lease, no claim and no DLQ. Keeping that token would have manufactured a collision with the parallel slice for no reason. If a later slice takes up candidate (a) or (b), retry-liveness returns with it.
_evidence_rules: Re-verify on synced main before coding: the live migration tail (0024 assumes 0023 — if it moved, renumber the file AND this manifest's merged_probe and the backlog entry BEFORE scope-gate register), the exact text of sessions_vis_chk and sessions_slots_chk, and that sessions.slots_max is still nullable with visibility still NOT NULL DEFAULT 'private'. Read feature_session_management_tech.md:120 verbatim — that line is the authority this slice acts on, and if its status has changed from 'hardening candidate ... chưa thuộc scope slice nào' the premise has changed. Read :386 too, because it is the behaviour this constraint makes unreachable. Do not modify an applied migration to make numbering tidy, and do not assume NOT VALID followed by VALIDATE is safe on populated tables — see design probe item (a). NOTE on dep_checks (corrected before authorization): an ack_outbox_event/0023 entry was dropped. dep_checks exist to catch UPSTREAM INTERFACE DRIFT, so every entry must name something this slice actually consumes; 0023 is merely the current migration tail and this slice consumes nothing from it. A dep_check on an unused symbol is worse than none — it fires on unrelated upstream edits, and a check that cries wolf gets ignored precisely when it is right. The two entries that remain (sessions_vis_chk, sessions_slots_chk) are the real contract: _scope_out promises neither is weakened, so if either disappears from schema.ts the premise has changed.
